replacement.title: Change jobs when the puck changes teams
replacement.objective: Update defensive responsibility after a turnover instead of continuing an attacking route.
replacement.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. YOU are navy. Gold F1 has just won the puck and now attacks the left net. The coach asks navy D1 to slow F1 while YOU find the separate gold runner F2. The turnover and assignments are given facts.
cues: D1 is asked to slow F1 while YOU locate F2.

sources.section: U11 Skills Matrix, printed page 22 (PDF page 22)

replacement.limits: Static original practice illustration; movement and outcomes are not simulated. The matrix supports tracking and basic team defence topics. The turnover and role split are authored assumptions; no recovery speed is shown. Position references are examples, not graded target zones.

questions.prompt: Which fact tells YOU that the previous attacking plan needs updating?

options.text: The right net is still visible.
Gold F1 now owns the puck and attacks the left net.

questions.explanation: Possession has changed to gold, whose attack direction is toward the left net. YOU are navy and must read the resulting defensive situation.

questions.prompt: Which cues matter for YOU’s new job in this rep?

options.text: F2’s route toward the left end
D1’s ability to slow the carrier
The old plan to receive a navy attacking pass

questions.explanation: The carrier pressure and separate runner are current cues. The old attacking plan can become useful again after a regain, but it does not describe this freeze.

questions.prompt: Put this suggested turnover response in order.

options.text: Notice which team now controls the puck.
Identify the pressure teammate and the separate runner.
Recover toward the defended end while checking for a pass.

questions.explanation: Recognizing possession first prevents continuing the old route by habit. Identifying both roles helps the recovery serve the current play.

questions.prompt: Move navy YOU toward a recovery position on the left-net side of gold F2. Explain what you would watch while moving.
questions.explanation: The reference is closer to the defended left end than F2, between F2’s side and the middle. Several routes may work; the carrier, D1 and actual speed affect whether YOU can reach this relationship.

questions.prompt: Suppose D1 wins the puck back cleanly before F2 receives. What changes first?

options.text: Recognize the new navy possession and look for support space.
Continue defending F2 without checking the puck.
Continue the old attacking route without finding D1

questions.explanation: Another possession change creates another read. YOU may offer a pass or protect against pressure depending on where D1 wins it; the drill does not require one automatic outlet.

questions.prompt: Explain how the same skater can have two different jobs within a few seconds here.
questions.explanation: Before the turnover YOU could support a navy attack. After it, YOU recover against a gold runner while D1 pressures the carrier. The reason is the changed possession and assignment, not a change in jersey or permanent position.

questions.prompt: What should YOU say when D1 wins the puck?

options.text: Turnover: D1 has it; find F2 and the left-net route

questions.explanation: The call names possession and the new defensive read.

questions.prompt: Which two changes define the job switch?
questions.explanation: Direction and the next attacker make the defensive job current; the old role is background information.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the left-net side of F2.
questions.explanation: This point moves toward the new gold attack and keeps F2 in view.

questions.prompt: F1 wins the puck back before F2 receives. Explain the next switch.
questions.explanation: Confirm F1 is now the carrier, then return to attacking support while checking D1 and F2.
